purpose: Meticulous re-review of coordinated or potentially coordinated hand contact and manipulation following user feedback on multimeter task.
required_checks: Each hand anatomical identity and contact part
Support versus proximity and active manipulation

reviews.previous_prompt: The robot uses its left hand to grasp the brown potato on the blue plate and lift it clear. It carries the potato across to the yellow plate, opens its fingers to release it onto the plate, and raises its empty hand. The right hand moves aside to make room for the placement. It carries the potato to the yellow plate while its right hand moves outward from above the plate to the plate's right side. The left hand lowers the potato and opens its fingers to release it onto the plate, ending open above the potato. Keep the camera fixed; preserve robot geometry, physically valid joint motion, and normal gripper opening and closing.

second_review.scope: Dedicated same-video second pass tracing both hands, load-bearing contacts, right-hand clearing timing, anatomical evidence and terminal release.

Thumb and fingers curl around opposite sides of the potato body; enclosing grasp established by 68-72.
Sustained one-hand potato grasp during lift/transport/lowering. No loaded regrasp, no grasp of a mechanism or separate part.
Fingers lift away and thumb opens; enclosing contact ends and plate receives the potato.
Open hand above released potato; residual projected thumb overlap may hide grazing contact, but no renewed grasp or lift.

Moves outward beside the plate during transport and before release; no potato grasp/contact or plate-rim grasp visible.

second_review.object_relative_comparison: Yellow rim and central objects serve as landmarks. Right palm and wrist shift outward relative to the yellow rim from 80 through 106, before the left fingers open at 110-113. Potato body remains between the left thumb and fingers through 109, then stays in the plate as the left fingers move apart. No independent articulated mechanism is present.
second_review.findings: Confirms a single-left-hand transfer with an unloaded right-hand clearing movement. Refines timing from the first review: outward movement is visible during transport, before lowering/release. Prompt now states this timing rather than describing right movement after the placement sentence.
uncertainties: The left palm hides some initial fingertip contacts while establishing the grasp; no separate lifted regrasp is observed.
The potato underside is occluded during lowering, so the exact first plate-contact frame cannot be fixed; complete release and retention inside the plate are visible.

During opening and settling, the projected left thumb partly overlaps the potato. Every final grazing contact cannot be determined from the camera angle, but there is no renewed enclosing grasp or lift.
Shoulder attachments are outside the image; anatomy is established from the paired near-side forearms and mirrored thumb/palm arrangement, consistent with the original instruction.
Whether the potato-shaped object is actual food or a replica cannot be determined visually.
